Read replicas

A read replica is a copy of your primary node that receives changes asynchronously and serves read-only queries. Replicas let you scale reads horizontally, keep reporting jobs away from the primary, and place data closer to users in other regions.

Because replication is asynchronous, a replica can lag behind the primary by a few milliseconds, or by several seconds under heavy write load. Applications that must read their own writes should send those reads to the primary, or use the wait_for_lsn option described below.

Creating a replica​

Start a new node with the --replica-of flag, pointing at the primary’s replication address. The node copies a snapshot first, and then streams the write-ahead log from the point where the snapshot was taken.

tidewater serve --data /var/lib/tw-replica \
  --replica-of primary.internal:7070

Monitoring lag​

Each replica exports a replication_lag_seconds metric. We suggest alerting when lag stays above ten seconds for more than five minutes, since short spikes during bulk loads are normal and usually clear on their own.

tip

Replicas never accept writes, so a misrouted write fails fast with error TW-4031 instead of silently diverging.
